strengths: The writing is consistently excellent — every moment in the transcripts lands with quiet weight, and the binary choices feel real rather than gamey ('Tell the truth. They deserve it.' vs 'Spare them.'). A newcomer feels the stakes immediately.
The heir identity line ('You are no longer Ottilie. You are Junia, her daughter — born into the world she left behind.') is now explicit and clear; succession is no longer a confusing hard cut.
The mechanic text on the title now says 'a choice between two paths, and it cannot be undone' — the permanence is front-and-centre, which correctly frames the emotional register before play starts.
The pulse dot on the pace text ('the years are passing') is a genuinely good liveness signal — it shows a first-timer that something is actively happening, not that the game is broken.
Hint duration at 13s is long enough to actually read; the seenChron hint triggering a beckon animation on the constellation link is a smart way to direct the eye without interrupting play.
The log tappability hint fires correctly and the beckon glow on the log is a useful affordance cue.
The constellation and chronicle are genuinely rewarding once found — star strands, chosen vs road-not-taken distinction, ancestor bios. For a curious newcomer who discovers them these are high-value.
Heirlooms, epitaphs, and the motto system give the dynasty tangible shape — by gen 3 in the Lindqvist transcript, the inherited 'soft spot for strays' already feels like family character.
blockers: The dynasty hook ('.lead' paragraph) is not reliably visible in the title screen layout. The screenshot confirms: the art overlay occupies the top portion, the tagline sits below it, and then 'Years pass on their own... Nothing can be undone.' appears — but the lead paragraph ('Each life hands the next its name...') is not visible above the rule. Whether due to art height, sheet compression, or a viewport edge case, a first-timer on a real device may never read the one sentence that explains why dynasty matters. The fix is in the HTML but does not reliably surface.

The long idle gap between moments remains unexplained to a newcomer who has already dismissed the intro hint. The hint fires once at 1.6s after starting, then fades after 13s. If a player pauses and returns 10 minutes later, or if they hit a quiet stretch from age 30 to 55 with no moments, there is no repeated signal that waiting is the game. The first-timer blockers from round 2 on the 'ambiguous waiting gap' are partially addressed but not closed.

The Chronicle and Constellation in-game links are still low-discoverability for a newcomer who ignores the hint. 'the chronicle ↗' is rendered at 9.5px in var(--ink-faint) at opacity 0.8 — that is genuinely difficult to read, and it sits in the top-right corner where a first-timer's eye is not naturally drawn. A player who dismisses or misses the seenChron hint has no second chance to discover the Chronicle until they already know to look.

improvements.what: Move the dynasty lead text above the art area, or ensure it is visible by making the art panel shorter (e.g. cap veil-art height at 35vh) on the title screen so the lead paragraph is always in the visible sheet area without scrolling.
improvements.why: The dynasty hook is the entire emotional reason to keep playing past one life. If it is not seen on the title, a first-timer has no frame for why the heir matters — which is the exact blocker from round 2.

improvements.what: Add a second ambient hint after ~10 minutes of play (or after age 40 passes with no decision), gated by a separate localStorage key, reminding the player that quiet years are normal: 'Long stretches with no moment to face are part of the life. The years are still passing.'
improvements.why: The single intro hint fades in 13s and is not repeated. A confused player who returns after a pause has no signal that the wait is intentional. This closes the 'ambiguous waiting gap' blocker without cluttering the first-timer experience.

improvements.what: Increase the chronicle link font-size to at least 11px and opacity to 1.0 (or near it), or give it a subtle amber underline on first play so it reads as a link rather than a label.
improvements.why: 'the chronicle ↗' at 9.5px and 80% opacity is nearly invisible at arm's length on mobile. It is one of the three elements the first-timer profile found hardest to discover last round. The constellation link at 0.9 opacity is readable; the chronicle link should match it.

improvements.what: On the heir screen, after the identity line, add one sentence summarising what was inherited in plain terms before the player hits 'Live this life' — e.g., 'Junia inherits the family's modest means, a warm name in the neighbourhood, and a soft spot for animals.' Currently this exists as the dim heirInherit paragraph but the inheritance framing is dense. A first-timer needs one punchy line that says 'this matters, and it came from you.'
improvements.why: The continuity between lives is the game's core mechanic and emotional hook. A first-timer who breezes through the heir screen without reading the inheritance paragraph misses the chain.

verdict: A Life has genuine literary quality and the round-3 fixes show real care — the heir identity line and the liveness dot are solid improvements — but the dynasty hook remains unreliably visible on the title screen, the waiting gap is only partially addressed, and the Chronicle link is still too dim to discover without a hint, which means a first-timer can still leave before understanding what kind of game they are playing.
